problem: Which of the following lines is perpendicular to $x+3y=6?$
worked_solution:
For the two lines to be perpendicular, their slopes must multiply to $-1.$

To find the slope of the given line $x+3y=6,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3y & =6 \\ 3y & =-x+6 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{3}x+2\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope of the given line is $-\frac{1}{3}.$

Looking at the answer choices, the line $y=3x$ has a slope of $3.$

Multiplying the slopes together, we have

$$
(-\frac{1}{3})\cdot 3=-1.
$$

Since the slopes multiply to $-1,$ we conclude that the line $y=3x$ is perpendicular to the given line.
